summary.en: Pakistan Army has struck and destroyed Afghan Taliban border posts after Taliban mortar and small-arms fire hit northwest Pakistan, killing a civilian and wounding five. The Taliban’s attack prompted a Pakistani operation against illegal Afghans in Peshawar and a call for international responsibility for Afghan refugees, while a UN expert criticised the Taliban’s rights record. Pakistan also closed the Iran-Iraq land border for pilgrims, linking the move to rising LPG prices, and China and Pakistan opened a green trade channel at the Sost-Khunjerab crossing. The conflict has caused 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Pakistans hær har slått til og ødelagt afghanske Taliban-grenseposter etter at Taliban avfyrte mortere og lett skytevåpen mot nordvestlige Pakistan, noe som drepte en sivil og såret fem. Talibans angrep førte til en pakistansk operasjon mot ulovlige afghanere i Peshawar og en oppfordring til internasjonalt ansvar for afghanske flyktninger, mens en FN-ekspert kritiserte Talibans menneskerettighetsrekord. Pakistan stengte også den iranske-irakiske landegrensen for pilegrimer, og knyttet tiltaket til stigende LPG-priser, og Kina og Pakistan åpnet en grønn handelskanal ved Sost-Khunjerab-overgangen. Konflikten har forårsaket 1 794 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
